clue.text: The earliest you can answer appeal quietly

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A
SA is the old abbreviation for sex appeal
P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to respond to a plea promptly and without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: SA for 'appeal' is a crossword staple: it stands for sex appeal, a dated euphemism also known as 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials stand for 'as soon as possible', an adverbial phrase for doing something at the first opportunity.

clue.text: Arab troubled by us aid

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the two words beside it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An Arab is bothered by American financial assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the letters of 'us aid'; 'by' merely joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the kingdom on the Arabian peninsula is an example of an Arab.

clue.text: American player in jug

definitions.meaning: in baseball, the US national game, the one who throws the ball to the batter
a large vessel with a handle and lip for pouring water or beer

explanation.surface: A sportsman from the States ends up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The same noun names both baseball's ball-thrower and a large pouring vessel.

clue.text: Nag firmly established couple

parts.note: something stable is steady and firmly established
as a verb, to couple is to mate

explanation.surface: Someone pesters a long-settled pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb meaning pester, but it is a noun for a horse; 'couple' is the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse kept in the same yard as another is one such; a nag is a horse, so this is a loose example.

clue.text: Styled as tailor? About right

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the letter for right
styled means shaped or fashioned, so the two words after it are refashioned

explanation.surface: Asked whether something was cut the way a tailor would do it, someone says that is roughly so.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'Styled' rearranges AS TAILOR into SATORIAL and 'About' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to tailoring or clothes, so 'styled as a tailor would' is about right.

clue.text: Loving party in first-class arena

indicators.note: in places the word for party inside the letters for first-class and arena

parts.note: A is the top grade, so first-class
a ring is an arena for boxing or a circus
a do is British informal for a party

explanation.surface: Someone is enjoying a celebration held in a top-quality stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loving' looks like a verb with 'party' as its object, but it is the adjective being defined, and 'in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for showing deep affection or worship.

clue.text: Miss old rope

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman, a lass
O is the abbreviation for old, as in OT for Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone feels nostalgic for a worn length of cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' reads as a verb meaning to pine for, but it is a noun for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a kind of rope with a noose, used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Give authority to member, one not entirely old-fashioned

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for old-fashioned is used without its last letter

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A club hands power to one of its number who is slightly behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final D from DATED, leaving DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to authorise or empower someone to act.

clue.text: Three in order overlook what's next? Reportedly so

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that overlooks another stands above it
putting the letters of the number in order means arranging them afresh
reportedly means as spoken, so the number that follows is heard and spelt another way

parts.note: four is the number that comes next after three

explanation.surface: A trio lined up in sequence fail to spot what is coming, or so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'what's next?' asks for the number following the one just named; 'in order', 'overlook' and 'Reportedly' are the signals, and the small word 'so' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning consequently or for that reason.

clue.text: Balls turn and one's tense in play

indicators.note: in play means in motion, so the letters of the words before it are moved about

explanation.surface: In a cricket match the deliveries start to spin and a batsman is nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges TURN and ONE'S TENSE; 'and' only joins the fodder. 'Balls' is British slang for rubbish, not the cricket deliveries the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, balls is an exclamation for complete rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Marches banned in south coast resort? Correct

indicators.note: marches are border regions, so banning them strips the borders, the first and last letters, from the resort

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: A seaside town on the Channel is confirmed to have outlawed protest parades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marches banned in' removes the first and last letters, B and N, from BRIGHTON, an English seaside town. Marches are borderlands, as in the Welsh Marches.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal British interjection of agreement, as is 'correct' said in assent.

clue.text: Not an immediate promise of marriage from great admirer

parts.note: I do is the vow spoken at a wedding
something not immediate comes later

explanation.surface: A devoted fan offers a wedding proposal, though not one for right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the second piece first: a marriage promise that is not immediate would be the vow followed by a word for afterwards. 'from' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a worshipper of idols, and so someone who admires excessively.

clue.text: Cultivation of remote dynasty

parts.note: far means distant or remote
the Ming were a Chinese imperial dynasty

explanation.surface: A distant royal house had a refined culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name agriculture, the working of land to grow crops.

clue.text: Cabaret that surprises greatly and how!

parts.note: to floor someone is to astonish them, so 'surprises greatly' is the verb in the third person

explanation.surface: A nightclub act astonishes its audience, and then some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' and 'and' are link words; 'how' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: It is entertainment performed among the tables at a nightclub, which is what a cabaret is.

clue.text: Heard copper so long

indicators.note: heard means the letters of the symbol for copper are spoken one by one and written as words

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone listened to a policeman for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' has the chemical symbol CU spoken letter by letter. 'copper' suggests a police officer and 'so long' a length of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal farewells.

clue.text: Flight is scariest in turbulence, enthralling all initially

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the rearranged letters hold the single letter inside them
turbulence is violent disturbance, so the letters of the word before it are shaken into a new order
initially means only the opening letter of the word before it is used

explanation.surface: Air travel is at its most frightening in rough weather, gripping every passenger from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is a set of steps, not air travel; 'is' links it to the wordplay, where 'in turbulence' and 'enthralling' and 'initially' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of steps between floors, a synonym here.

clue.text: Travel period reduced? That's the absolute truth

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: reduced means the word for period is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: Asked whether the journey time has been cut, someone swears it has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the final L from SPELL; 'That's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Used figuratively it means something accepted as unquestionably true, as in 'take it as'.

clue.text: Nice little hotel is what oldies may have earned

definitions.meaning: Nice is the French city, where a small boarding house goes by this French word
the regular income paid to retired people after their working lives

explanation.surface: A pleasant small guesthouse is the reward retired folk deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, signalling a French word for a small boarding house; 'is' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Continental boarding house and a retirement income.

clue.text: Mabel's beaten after spades and hearts shuffle

indicators.note: after places the rearranged name behind the two suit letters

parts.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the name without its possessive ending

explanation.surface: At the card table Mabel loses once two suits have been mixed into the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffle' is a way of walking, not what you do to cards; 'beaten' and 'after' are the signals, and the possessive ending on the name is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to walk awkwardly, dragging the feet.

clue.text: Is poor car getting a run out abroad a ford model?

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
out tells you the letters for 'a run' are taken out of the three words

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a clapped-out motor taken for a drive overseas is a Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes A and R from IS POOR CAR, leaving ISPOOCR, which 'abroad' rearranges. The Ford in question was a large saloon sold in Britain and Europe from 1985.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a Ford executive saloon, the Granada's successor, so an example of the make's models.

clue.text: They could reproduce bats

definitions.meaning: bonk is British slang for have sex, so people doing it might produce offspring
bats is informal for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Flying mammals of the night are capable of breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' is the slang adjective for mad, not the animal. The first definition is a joke on 'bonk', British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for crazy and, read as a plural noun, people having sex.

clue.text: Look after famous engineer with Italian red wine

indicators.note: after places the word for look behind the engineer's name

parts.note: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the Victorian engineer of British railways, bridges and ships
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone takes care of a celebrated engineer and brings a bottle of Chianti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'take care of', but 'after' is only a position word and 'with' a link; the engineer built the Great Western Railway.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Tuscan red made at Montalcino, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Rolls is entering for nothing in parking areas

indicators.note: entering for means the word 'is' goes in to take the place of the letter for nothing

parts.note: lots are areas for parking cars, in American usage
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A luxury car gets into car parks without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering for' swaps the O of LOTS for IS. 'Rolls' suggests a Rolls-Royce, but it means registers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plural nouns for registers of names, as in an electoral roll.

clue.text: Lustful Romeo having been bedded was exhausted

indicators.note: bedded means embedded, so the letter for Romeo is planted inside the word for lustful

parts.note: randy is British informal for lustful
Romeo is the word for R in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: An amorous lover was worn out after a night of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been bedded' puts R inside RANDY. 'exhausted' means used up, as a well is, not tired.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that gave out completely did this; the phrase is an idiom for being used up.

clue.text: Gag about small person? Censor it!

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to censor is to cut out, so the word 'it' is cut from the word for a small person

parts.note: titch is British informal for a small person

explanation.surface: A joke at a short man's expense is ordered to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Censor' cuts IT from TITCH, leaving TCH. 'Gag' looks like a joke but is the verb meaning to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to heave as if about to vomit.

clue.text: They should succeed perhaps in English art work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or manipulate it, so the letters before it are manipulated

explanation.surface: Some painters may well do well with a piece in a British style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges PERHAPS IN, E and ART together. 'succeed' means inherit a title, not prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: They are those first in line to inherit a throne or title, so expected to come next.

clue.text: Is new remix one of Jagger's band brought about, rock creating a stink?

indicators.note: brought about means the band member is placed around the rearranged letters

parts.note: Mick Jagger sings with the Rolling Stones, so one member is a Stone

indicators.note: a remix is a fresh mixing, so the letters of the two words before it are mixed again

explanation.surface: A fresh version of a track by a Rolling Stone causes an uproar in the music world.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'rock' is geological, not musical; 'remix' and 'brought about' are the signals, and the surface's music-business story is all misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a limestone, also called stinkstone, that gives off a foul smell when struck or rubbed.

clue.text: London area broadcast excited but tails off

indicators.note: tails off means each of the two words loses its last letter, its tail

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
hot can mean excited or worked up

explanation.surface: A programme from the capital started thrillingly and then petered out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tails off' drops the W of SOW and the T of HOT; 'but' is a link. 'broadcast' is the farming sense of scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a district of the West End, known for restaurants and nightlife.
